task.description: Diagnose and prepare a fix for GH #576 (ISS-0622): quota_enforcement.zig reads PER_TENANT usage tables (instance_projections, instance_waits, dead_letter_items) unqualified via a pool connection, which fails for every tenant under .LEGACY_RLS storage mode (the default). docs/issues/ISS-0622.json ALREADY CONTAINS a full root_cause_analysis, verification_method, and acceptance_criteria from this issue's original filing (discovered incidentally during WF03-GH566-20260808/ISS-0617's implementation) -- read it first via fn:search-issues / direct read, confirm it is still accurate (source code may have moved since filing), and do NOT re-diagnose from scratch if it holds up. The issue's own acceptance_criteria explicitly says a design decision is needed: (a) resolve storage_mode explicitly in quota_enforcement.zig and issue schema-qualified queries (tenant_default.<table> for LEGACY_RLS tenants), or (b) create public-schema equivalents/views for these three tables so both storage modes can read them unqualified, or (c) some other approach. This decision needs CODE-DESIGNER analysis -- do not implement inline, route it through Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER) with full context. Also check: does any OTHER middleware share this same unqualified-read-via-pool-under-LEGACY_RLS pattern against PER_TENANT-only tables? (ISS-0622's acceptance_criteria explicitly asks this -- a broader audit may be warranted, but stay within THIS issue's scope: fix quota_enforcement.zig, note findings about siblings for a future issue if any are found, don't fix them here unless truly trivial and directly required).
acceptance_criteria: ISS-0622s existing root_cause_analysis confirmed still accurate (or updated if source moved)
Fix strategy decision made and documented (schema-qualify vs public-view vs other) with rationale
Routed to CODE-DESIGNER (Step 2) with full context, not implemented directly by ISSUE-FIXER
Any sibling middleware sharing the same pattern noted (not fixed unless trivial and in-scope)
